plan.planning_summary: This portfolio tests three distinct physical approaches to achieving dual-band spectral performance (high UV reflection, high SWIR transmission) within a 30-layer HfO2/SiO2 constraint on fused silica. Route 1 tests whether a classic periodic quarter-wave Bragg stack centered on the UV band can achieve sufficient SWIR transmission as a baseline. Route 2 tests whether chirping layer thicknesses through the stack broadens the UV reflection band without degrading SWIR transmission. Route 3 tests whether introducing a defect cavity layer creates a transmission resonance in the SWIR band while maintaining UV reflection. These axes are genuinely distinct: periodic vs. graded vs. cavity-enhanced topologies explore different interference mechanisms. Literature L01 and L03 support the HfO2/SiO2 material system choice; L02 supports the optimization approach; L22 supports dichroic design principles. No route claims validation from literature - all performance is determined by the solver.

routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave optical thickness layers at the center wavelength of the reflection band create constructive interference for reflection. Outside the stopband, the stack becomes increasingly transparent as wavelength increases, potentially allowing SWIR transmission.
